sites.name: IM-2 Athena landing point (Mons Mouton region)
sites.coordinate_frame: Lunar Mean Earth/polar axis (ME) body-fixed frame, planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude. ASSUMED: the LROC page does not name its frame; LRO products use the ME frame by project convention. Horizons interprets the submitted coordinates in MOON_ME (DE421-based).
sites.coordinate_source_title: LROC: IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely (M. Robinson, 10 March 2025) - gives 84.7906° S, 29.1957° E
sites.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km LOLA reference sphere, LDEM_80S_20M (PDS LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0 V2.0) bilinear at the site; consistent with 1131 LOLA RDR shots within ~600 m (DEM - shot mean -0.26 m, sd 0.67 m). The DEM was gridded from LOLA RDR shots, so this checks our reading of the product (scaling, reference, projection, interpolation), not the terrain independently. See data/terrain/im2-athena_site_elevation_report.json.
sites.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as LOLA heights.
sites.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (5321.9 m + 1 m) / 1000 = 5.3229 km. Both heights are relative to the same 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Rounding: the bilinear LDEM_80S_20M surface is 5321.8804 m; it was rounded to 0.1 m (5321.9 m) before forming the Horizons altitude, so the submitted point is 1.0196 m above the interpolated surface (nominal 1 m). The terrain horizon uses the same submitted point, so Sun/Earth directions and skyline refer to one observer. Measured effect of the 0.0196 m: skyline <= 0.0034 deg (nearest skyline point 330 m), 1 of 8640 Sun steps (2026-12-30 sunset, one 10-minute step), no demo-window metric change; Sun/Earth directions ~3e-9 deg. No absolute vertical accuracy of the surface value is claimed: LOLA RDR shots near the site (the DEM's own source data) agree with the DEM to mean -0.26 m, sd 0.67 m, max |4.71| m (1131 shots within ~600 m), and the 8 shots within 30 m span 5321.75-5322.69 m; these are consistency and local-spread figures, not an accuracy. Terrain within 100 m of the coordinate spans -4.4 to +4.6 m (a height range, not an uncertainty; the coordinate's accuracy is not stated). Horizons echo: Center geodetic 5.3229 km exactly; |Center cylindric| = 1742.7228895 km, 10.5 mm below 1737.4 + 5.3229 km, explained by the printed precision (Dz is given to 0.1 m), so the echo confirms the radius only to about +/-5 cm.

sites.coordinate_frame: ME/DE421 body-fixed, planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude, following cached LOLA labels; equivalence to source coordinate frame not demonstrated. ASSUMED: NASA section 7.3.3 and Figure 0.1 do not specify the frame realization or latitude type for this tuple.

sites.coordinate_source_product: ACD-50044 Revision A, NTRS 20230007818, section 7.3.3 p.46; Figure 0.1 p.38
sites.point_description: study location / hypothetical landing point; not an observed landing or a designated mission destination
sites.coordinate_accuracy_note: not stated; published decimal places are not a measured uncertainty
sites.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km LOLA reference sphere, LDEM_80S_20M V2.0, bilinear at the published point interpreted in ME. Rounded to 0.1 m. Absolute vertical accuracy and source-frame equivalence are not established. No local RDR shot consistency check performed. See data/terrain/connecting-ridge-cr1_site_elevation_report.json.
sites.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as LOLA heights. Submitted 2026-11-14 (milestone 4C).
sites.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (1941.8 m + 1 m) / 1000 = 1.9428 km. Both heights are relative to the same 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Rounding: the bilinear LDEM_80S_20M surface is 1941.8206 m; it was rounded to 0.1 m (1941.8 m) before forming the Horizons altitude, so the submitted point is 0.9794 m above the interpolated surface (nominal 1 m, 0.0206 m lower). The terrain horizon uses the same submitted point (r = 1737.4 km + 1942.8 m), so Sun/Earth directions and skyline refer to one observer. No absolute vertical accuracy of the surface value is claimed; no local LOLA RDR shot consistency check was made at the site point; the nearest 20 m DEM pixel has no LOLA shot (interpolated height). Horizons echo (all 12 responses): Center geodetic 222.6, -89.468, 1.9428 exactly; Center cylindric Dxy 16.14983 km and Dz -1739.268 km equal the submitted point rounded to the printed 5 and 3 decimals, so |r| (177 mm above 1737.4 + 1.9428 km as printed) confirms the radius only to about +/-0.5 m, the printed precision of Dz near the pole.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus landing point (Malapert A region)
sites.coordinate_frame: MOON_ME body-fixed frame (the kernel's MOON_ME is an alias for MOON_ME_DE440_ME421, closely aligned with the DE421 mean Earth/polar axis frame), planetodetic coordinates on a 1737.4 km sphere (= planetocentric for a sphere), east-positive longitude. The kernel states the frame; it does not state the coordinate's source or accuracy.
sites.coordinate_source_title: NAIF CLPS IM-1 frames kernel clps_to2im_im1_v02.tf (Version 2, 2025-08-22): IM1_LANDING_SITE at latitude -80.12759, longitude 1.44587 deg, MOON_ME
sites.coordinate_source_product: clps_to2im_im1_v02.tf (NAIF PDS4 CLPS SPICE archive); cross-check: LROC featured image 1360 (2024-02-26) gives 80.13 S, 1.44 E
sites.point_description: where Intuitive Machines' IM-1 Odysseus lander came to rest on 2024-02-22 (it landed tilted on a slope)
sites.coordinate_accuracy_note: not stated by the kernel; LROC's two-decimal value agrees to its rounding (0.005 deg of latitude is about 150 m)
sites.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km LOLA reference sphere, LDEM_80S_20M V2.0, bilinear at the kernel's point interpreted in ME. Rounded to 0.1 m. LDEM_75S_60M gives 2592.30 m. The point is about 4 km inside the 20 m product's edge. No local LOLA RDR shot consistency check performed. See data/terrain/im1-odysseus_site_elevation_report.json.
sites.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as LOLA heights.
sites.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (2593.5 m + 1 m) / 1000 = 2.5945 km. Both heights are relative to the 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Rounding: the bilinear LDEM_80S_20M surface is 2593.53 m; it was rounded to 0.1 m before forming the altitude, so the submitted point is 0.9716 m above the interpolated surface (nominal 1 m). The NAIF kernel lists an altitude of 2.583 km for its site point (10.5 m lower; its basis is not stated); it is not used. The generic terrain horizon and rendering use this same configured observer; no observer substitution is made.

terrain.source: PDS Geosciences Node, LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, polar products V2.0 (LOLA data through 2017-02-02)
terrain.rule: Use LDEM_80S_20M wherever the ray is inside it; continue rays that leave it (azimuths ~320-351 deg, 165-190 km) in LDEM_75S_60M. Stop a ray only when terrain at the global LOLA maximum height (+100 m) could no longer exceed the running horizon. If a ray leaves every file first, that azimuth's horizon is null (unknown), never flat.
